business_summary: Ather Energy is an automobiles company. Revenue grew 27.28% a year over three years to FY26, but the company is loss-making. FY26 net profit was -517.17 Rs cr, and all of the last four quarters were losses. Operating margin is -11.12%, and debt/equity is 0.26x.
why_own: The case rests on revenue growing at a healthy rate while operating losses narrow, with operating margin up 28.61 pp over three years. Evidence is thin: the company is loss-making, there are no profit-based valuation or return metrics, and no investor documents were supplied, so the drivers below are metric-only.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a healthy double-digit rate (3-year CAGR was 27.28% to FY26).
Operating losses keep narrowing toward breakeven. Operating margin is -11.12%, after improving 28.61 pp over three years.
The balance sheet stays lightly leveraged while the company is loss-making (debt/equity is 0.26x). (warn line tightened by code from 0.5 to 0.34.)
Interest cover should stay above 1.5x. (added by code: currently -5.29.)
Trailing four-quarter net profit should not be negative. (added by code: currently -389.84.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin deteriorates materially below the current -11.12%, so losses are widening instead of narrowing.
Revenue growth slows sharply, undermining the growth case that justifies the current losses.
Leverage rises to a level that is risky for a company with negative interest cover.

risks.statement: The company is loss-making: FY26 net profit was -517.17 Rs cr, trailing four-quarter net profit was -389.84 Rs cr, and all of the last four quarters were losses.
Returns and debt servicing are negative: ROCE is -13.44% and interest cover is -5.29x. ROE and cash flow/profit cannot be measured because profit is not positive.
The stock trades at 22.03x book value with no positive earnings to anchor valuation. P/E and P/E versus history cannot be computed, so the price depends on future profitability that is not yet shown.
The 5-year revenue CAGR of 115.07% is much higher than the 3-year CAGR of 27.28%, so growth has slowed over the longer window. The reason for the gap is untested here.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if revenue growth is already decelerating and losses stop narrowing. Neither would show up in the thresholds. Operating margin is still -11.12%, net profit has been negative for four straight quarters, and interest cover is -5.29x. The stock trades at 22.03x book with no profit to anchor it. The kill lines are lenient: margin must fall to -25% (about 14 pp worse) and 3-year CAGR below 10%, which is under the 12% break line. The 3-year CAGR (27.28%) is a lagging figure and could hide a sharp recent slowdown. The 5-year CAGR of 115.07% shows the growth rate has already fallen a long way. Low leverage is the only comfort, and it says nothing about how losses are funded. What would change this view: Evidence of positive trailing four-quarter net profit or interest cover above 1.5x, together with revenue growth that holds above 20% on a current-year basis rather than only on a 3-year CAGR.
